newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal draft budget cuts deficit to 2.9 pct GDP.
newsitem.headline: Portugal draft budget cuts deficit to 2.9 pct GDP.

text.p: Portugal's 1997 draft budget sees savings of 200 billion escudos compared with 1996, with the deficit down to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) from an expected 4.3 percent this year, the Finance Ministry said.
The draft, which was being discussed with members of parliament on Friday, saw state spending rising 4.5 percent year-on-year, while receipts would rise nine percent.
The weight of state spending as a percentage of GDP would decline to 28.7 percent from 29 percent this year.

The government had already announced the macro-economic forecasts on which its budget was being based. These include economic growth next year of 2.75-3.25 percent, slightly higher than in 1996 and inflation of 2.0-2.25 percent, down from a forecast 3.0-3.5 percent in 1996.
The draft budget will be formally approved by the cabinet on Monday and then sent to parliament the following day.
The plan implies a "strong limitation" of public spending, the Finance Ministry said in a statement containing details of the blueprint.
The primary surplus, which is net of interest payments, would rise to 1.5 percent of GDP from 0.7 percent in 1996.

State spending on goods and services would actually fall as a results of tight controls being applied to the various ministries, it said. The Education Ministry would be one of the few ministries to see a rise in spending with expenditure being planned to grow 7.5 percent.
Debt interest payments would fall to 14.5 percent of GDP from 15.7 percent this year.

State investment would rise 10 percent in nominal terms to 441.3 billion escudos. Public consumption is seen rising more slowly than in 1996 at 0.75-1.25 percent while private consumption should rise 2.0-2.5 percent.
